topic: Curious facts about living on the equator
title: Living at the Middle of the World 🇪🇨🌍
hook: What's special about living right in the middle of the world?

scenes.narration: What's special about living right in the middle of the world?
The equator splits the Earth into two halves, and that line gave Ecuador its name.
There, the ground spins faster than anywhere else: about sixteen hundred and seventy kilometers per hour.
That spin makes the Earth bulge at the equator: its radius there is about twenty-one kilometers bigger.
That's why you weigh a little less there: about three hundred fifty grams less if you weigh seventy kilos.
Also, day and night each last about twelve hours, all year round.
And in March and September, at noon, the Sun is directly overhead and there's almost no shadow.
Beware the trick of water swirling differently on each side of the line: at that scale, Earth's rotation doesn't decide it.
And the famous Middle of the World monument isn't exactly on the line: GPS puts the equator about two hundred forty meters away.
Send this to someone who lives in Ecuador or wants to visit.

description: Ecuador is named after the equator. There the ground spins at about 1,670 km/h, Earth's radius is about 21 km bigger than at the poles, and you weigh about 0.5% less. Day and night last ~12 hours all year, and at the equinoxes there's almost no shadow at noon. The sink trick that swirls differently on each side is a myth, and the Middle of the World monument sits about 240 m from the GPS-measured line. Original 3D animation; exaggerated scale.

claims.statement: At the equator, Earth's surface rotates at about 1,670 km/h.
Earth's equatorial radius is about 21 km larger than its polar radius.
Effective gravity is ~9.780 m/s² at the equator and ~9.832 m/s² at the poles (≈0.5% less).
At the scale of a sink, the Coriolis effect is far too weak to decide which way the water spins.
The Ciudad Mitad del Mundo monument lies about 240 m from the equator according to GPS measurements.
